annotations.title: TIA — connect device to IO system

description: Assigns the interface of an IO device to the IO system of a controller interface. `interface` and `controllerInterface` are interface item names from tia_device_network (default: the primary network interface). The controller must already have an IO system (409 no_io_system: create it with tia_io_system_create) and the device interface must be on the SAME subnet as that IO system (409 cross_subnet_assignment, details.deviceSubnet and details.ioSystemSubnet: connect the device to that subnet with tia_network_connect first; 409 subnet_inventory_incomplete, details.gaps: the subnet of an IO system could not be read, so the check cannot be made). Also refused, nothing changed: 409 not_io_device, 409 already_assigned (the interface is on a DIFFERENT IO system: tia_io_system_disconnect first), 404 not_found; assigning it to the IO system it is already on is a no-op with changes:[]. The result carries `ioSystem`, `changes` and a `postcheck` (the serve re-reads the assignment after the write); a mismatch is 409 postcheck_failed (details.mismatches): re-read with tia_device_network. dryRun (Gd11) is answered by the serve (needs an open project): it runs the same guards and returns the plan WITHOUT changing anything. Maps to POST /iosystems/connect. M-off.

controller.description: name of the controller device (CPU) that owns the IO system

controllerInterface.description: controller interface item name, as listed by tia_device_network (default: the primary network interface)

dryRun.description: Gd11: plan-without-applying — validates the guards and describes the action WITHOUT mutating the project

interface.description: IO device interface item name, as listed by tia_device_network (default: the primary network interface)
